Rule: Invoice-amount check: runs only for a council whose file repeats one invoice total on every line of a transaction (Wokingham). Lines are grouped by transaction number and payee; the stated Gross is compared with the Net uplifted by the line's VAT Type label (Standard 20%, Reduced 5%, other labels 0%).
Rows whose payee is redacted (REDACT, 'personal data', NULL, '*Exclude') or whose transaction number is a redaction placeholder are left out and counted as redacted.

A payment run printed n-squared times that is still unexplained is reported on its distinct lines: its net, expected gross and gap are those of the de-duplicated lines (and of the transaction's redacted lines, stated in the detail), not of the repeated row total.

A transaction is listed only when the stated Gross differs from the VAT-uplifted Net by more than 1p; a gap of up to 5p is classed VAT rounding, under GBP 1 is classed small gap, GBP 1 or more is classed unreconciled.
Repeated-payment check: same payee, same net, same gross, same description and same payment date under two or more different transaction numbers.

Transactions with no published payment date are left out (two missing dates cannot be shown to be equal); redacted payees are left out; transaction numbers a spreadsheet has turned into scientific notation are treated as one transaction per row.
A group a standing schedule, a recurring batch or a catch-up cadence accounts for is still listed; the reading is shown beside it and the group stays in the open count.
Shared-number check: one transaction number with more than one payee or more than one payment date.
Redacted payees and redaction placeholders are left out, so a transaction number shared with a redacted line shows only its named lines.

same supplier, same lines (net and description), different transaction numbers (the same number in two files is one transaction published twice, not a twin), both first pay dates published and within 7 days, lines of that kind seen in at most three transactions; each transaction has one payee, at least two lines and a total of at least GBP 10,000; redacted payees, transaction numbers a spreadsheet has mangled, and transactions in which every line is listed an even number of times (a doubled listing) are left out
Each transaction has one payee, at least two lines and a total of at least GBP 10,000 (absolute).

Redacted payees, spreadsheet-mangled transaction numbers, and transactions in which every line is listed an even number of times (a doubled listing, counted separately in the file-duplication check) are left out.

A transaction number that appears in two files with the same lines is one transaction published twice, not two transaction numbers: it is not paired, it is listed in same_number_two_files.csv and counted by the cross-file check.
Extra copies are counted per group of identical transactions: a group of k transactions has k-1 extra copies, not one per pair.
A line (payee, net, description) listed at least twice under one transaction number, with an absolute net of at least GBP 10,000.
Redacted payees and spreadsheet-mangled transaction numbers are left out. Wokingham is not run: its invoice-amount check already tests each transaction against the published invoice total.
A row is 'also in an earlier file' when an earlier file holds a row with the same payee, amount, payment date, description and service.

The pay date is compared as a day (2025-08-28 and 28/08/2025 are the same day). Where one of the two rows has no published payee name, the published Supplier Number stands in for the name (Bradford 2025).
Redacted payees are left out. A standing monthly payment never matches because its payment date differs each month.
A file is flagged when at least 50 of its rows, at least 2% of it, and at least three times the 75th-percentile rate of up to five files either side (floored at 0.5%), are in an earlier file.
A row is an exact repeat when every published column matches another row in the same file (a number the council did not publish, and a per-row system timestamp, are not compared).
A file is flagged when at least 50 rows, at least 2% of the file, and at least three times the 75th-percentile repeat rate of up to five files either side (floored at 0.5%) are exact repeats.
Flows from a council to another council or to a company the council owns, as named in the hand-graded alias table (accepted grades only).

A council's payments to itself are left out. Rows with no published payment date count in every total and are shown in the undated columns; they are left out only of the year series and the month test.

'No return flow' needs at least three years and more than GBP 100,000 out with no credit row; 'return under 2%' needs the same with credits under 2% of the money out; a payment-misfit month needs at least twelve months of history, more than three times the median month, and more than GBP 100,000.
Debt ledger: a transaction whose description, cost centre or any other published column says debt, interest, loan or PWLB (the service heading is not searched).

Labels that contain a keyword but are not the council's own borrowing are removed first: debtors, deferred debt, stock loaned, student loan repayments, provisions for bad debts, debt collection and debt management, external interest payable headings, and similar named in the engine.
A payee spelling counts as another council or company only when its grade in the alias table is 'accept'; proposals scored by the matcher are not used until graded by hand.
Declared spend is compared with a council's file total only for a council-year whose twelve months are all published and for which the government's Revenue Outturn figure is held.
Payroll is not in the supplier ledger and is shown as declared but not compared.

A row is redacted when a payee-name column of the file (the payee column, or a second name column such as Supplier Name (alt)) carries a redaction marker. Every name column of that row is then replaced by the marker, in the export, the slices and every cross file, and only a hash of the name is kept. A marker in a purpose or identifier column does not withhold a payee the council names (a company paid for a purpose the council redacted).

A row the council gave no usable transaction number is shown as "(no number published) N" (N the row position, a method such as CHAPS after it): the scanner's own number, never presented as the council's.

Rows left out of the published files are listed in dropped.csv with a reason: a row with no payee and no payment date (a footer, total or blank line), or a line already published in an earlier file. A whole file the reader cannot open is named with its reason.
